## Summary

**LEA** (Load Effective Address).

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `<ea> → An` |
| Syntax | `LEA <ea>,Bn`<br>`LEA (Bn),An` |
| Description | Loads the effective address into an address register. |
| Constraints | No LEA (Bn),Bm or MOVEA.L Bn,Bm |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

LEA &lt;ea&gt;,Bn:

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–12 | `0100` |
| 1 | 11–9 | Bn |
| 1 | 8–6 | `101` |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |

LEA (Bn),An:

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–12 | `0100` |
| 1 | 11–9 | An |
| 1 | 8–3 | `111001` |
| 1 | 2–0 | Bn |

### Example

```asm
    lea    1(a0),b1
```

```text
ea a0: .. .. .. .. 00 12 34 56
Result:
bn b1: .. .. .. .. 00 12 34 57
```

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have LEA. This page covers only the 68080 addition: LEA with a B address register as destination, and LEA (Bn),An. For the classic forms, the Motorola manual applies.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T write LEA (Bn),Bm or MOVEA.L Bn,Bm: B to B is not supported.
